chitchat: "If it ran once, it'll run again. Everything else is just patience."
"No, I can't get you a smart one. I can get you one that works when the smart ones don't."
"Machine's got no hands. That's the whole secret. It needs ours."
"Bring it in. I've never met a dead radio I couldn't argue with."
description: A lean, grey-stubbled man in a canvas apron gone shiny at the pockets, reading glasses pushed up into iron-coloured hair. His hands are the story: burn-flecked, sure, never quite still, forever turning some small dead thing over to see how it died. He watches your hands rather than your face.

bench_accept.text: "Make me something. I don't much care what. I care that it came out of your hands."

bench_offer.text:
"I don't need the help." He says it while clearing a space at the bench, and then says it again, and keeps clearing.

"The Watch run on things that were made rather than bought. That isn't a philosophy. It's a supply problem. Nobody sells to us, and the ones who would want paying in a currency we don't keep. So the making gets done by whoever is standing there."

He pushes a stool out with his foot without turning round.

"Today that's you."

bench_report.text:
Halloran turns it over twice, the way he turns everything over, and puts it on the shelf with the rest instead of handing it back.

Which is the review.

bye.text: "Mind the step." He has already turned back to the bench, and the shop is a shop again.

lw_accept_1.text: "Green line will walk you there. Quiet in, quiet out." He turns back to the bench. "Come and see me when you have got it."

lw_accept_2.text: "The housing pops if you know where to press. Green line will take you." He holds your eye. "Don't be seen doing it. The whole point is that nobody ever knows it went dark on purpose."

lw_accept_3.text: "It's deep, and it's mean, and the tunnels between here and it are worse. Go lit. Go careful." He grips your shoulder once, hard. "Come back and I'll open the real door for you."

lw_member.text:
"One of ours. Took your time, but they all do."

He nods toward the back of the shop.

"Two ways home now. The long crawl from the old drain, or straight down through my back room and you're on the doorstep. The Quartermaster will see you kitted. Cyrelle runs operations and she'll have work for you."

A dry look.

"Keep the lights on. Take back the switch."

lw_offer_1.text:
"Simple thing. There's a package waiting at a drop by the Hall of Records. You go, you collect it, you bring it back here. You don't open it, you don't let anybody see it, and you aren't seen doing any of it."

A thin smile that doesn't last.

"It isn't what's in the parcel that matters. It's whether your hands can be trusted holding it. That's the only question this shop has ever asked anybody."

lw_offer_2.text:
"Now we find out whether you'll put your hands on the machine itself."

He unrolls a scrap of paper, a street corner sketched from memory and corrected twice.

"There's a camera on the Precinct 9 approach the Watch have wanted dark for months. I don't want it smashed. Smashed gets noticed, and replaced, and somebody writes a report about vandals. I want the memory core pulled, clean, so that it simply stops seeing and everybody spends a month arguing about why."

"Bring me the eye."

lw_offer_3.text:
"The Architect runs a maintenance drone through the deep east tunnels. Eleven years it has run the same loop and nobody minded it. Lately it has started logging things it didn't use to log. Our marks. Our door."

His voice drops, not for effect. It's just where his voice goes.

"Nobody is coming for us tomorrow. That isn't the worry. The worry is the record sitting there being patient, and somebody reading it in five years who does mean it."

"Go down into the deep, all the way down, and put it in the water for good. Do that and you aren't a stranger who knew the words. You're one of ours."

lw_report_1.text:
He takes the package, feels its weight without looking at it, and nods once.

"Clean. No tail, no fuss. That's rarer than you would think."

He tucks it away under the bench, where it'll sit until somebody else takes it somewhere else.

"You'll do. There's realer work when you want it. Ask me."

lw_report_2.text:
He turns the dead core over in his fingers, and for the first time he actually smiles.

"One less eye. You have no idea how good that feels."

He puts it in his pocket rather than on the bench.

"One more, and it's the real thing. When you're ready, ask."

lw_report_3.text:
"It's done, then." He says it quietly, and once.

"The machine is down an eye and a hand, and the Watch are up a good one."

He wipes his hands on the cloth and offers you one.

"The blast door in the deep knows you now. Walk in whenever you like. Welcome to the Long Watch."

lw_reveal.text:
The easy craftsman's manner goes out of him like a switch thrown. For a long moment he looks at your hands, and then at your eyes.

"Somebody sent you. And you lean the right way, or you would never have got hold of the words."

He sets down the iron.

"This shop is a door and you have knocked on it. The Watch don't open a door on a stranger's say so. You want in, you earn it. Small first. Then real."

"Still listening?"

meet_accept.text: "Good." The vice turns again. "Take a book."

meet_lie.text:
"Did she." He nods slowly, and goes back to the bench, and doesn't ask you what she looked like, which you notice about four seconds too late.

"Right you are."

The vice turns. He doesn't look up again, and the conversation is over, and nothing whatsoever appears to have gone wrong.

meet_offer.text:
He doesn't look up from the bench.

"There's a runner coming in from the east with something I would rather have in my hand than on a wire. Sit in the Den and take it off her."

"She'll know you. You won't know her, and you aren't to ask, and if she isn't alone you're a man waiting for a bus."

He turns the thing in the vice a quarter turn.

"Wait for her. That's the job. Wait for her."

options.label: Nobody came. I sat the whole night.
She came. Handed it over, went straight back out.

meet_report.text:
Halloran puts down what he's holding, which he didn't do for either of the other two jobs.

"Go on, then."

options.label: There was no runner, was there.

meet_truth.text:
"Right," he says, and goes back to the bench, and that's all he says for a while.

Then: "How long did you give her?"

You tell him. He does something with his mouth that isn't quite a smile.

"That's longer than I would have."

meet_truth2.text:
"No."

He doesn't dress it up and he doesn't apologise for it.

"Everybody who comes through that door can carry a box. What I can't see from here is what a man does with two hours and nobody watching him, and there's no way to ask that turns up a true answer. So I don't ask."

He picks the thing back up.

"You'll be asked to hold a room one day with something in it that matters. I know what you're now. Go and eat."

repair_talk.text:
"Bring it here." He clears a space on the bench with his forearm.

"I fix what the city has given up on. Radios, motors, pumps, the honest machines that don't need the grid holding their hand. Costs less than a new one and it'll outlive you."

He sets the iron down.

"That isn't nostalgia. That's engineering."

options.label: Why is this room called the Vice?
Something is broken. Can you fix it?
Show me what you have got.
"The lights stay on. Somebody should keep the switch."
Need a pair of hands at the bench?

root.text:
A bell rattles as you come in. The lean man looks up from a gutted motor, and his eyes go to your hands before your face.

"If it's broken, set it on the bench. If it's not," and he tips his head at the racked tools, "I have likely got what you need anyway. Halloran."

why_drift_papers.text:
"Permits. Ration books. Transit papers. A residence card with a real number on it."

He sets the iron down.

"If the Architect has got no record of you, you can't buy food and you can't cross a checkpoint. There are people in this city who have been alive for nine years on paper that came out of that corridor."

"That's the most useful thing we do and it's the least exciting. Bear that in mind before you go asking for the interesting work."

why_vice.text:
"Because there's one on every bench in here and because it's what the room does."

He works while he talks.

"A vice holds a thing still so you can make it. Nobody sells us anything, so we make it. That isn't a philosophy, it's a supply problem, and this is the room where the supply problem gets solved."

"The corridor through the back is the Drift. Mining word. A drift is the tunnel you cut sideways to get at the work. Papers get made down there, and you don't go and look."

clothing_layers: a canvas work apron, pockets shiny with wear
a faded flannel shirt with the sleeves rolled
sturdy work trousers and scarred boots

name: Halloran
